description: A bootstrap of another notation (engine §9). Each rule of the syntax document of the notation, except text, has a new name in turn. A renamed rule is a wrapper, and the reader reads through it. A rename in loads gives a dialect, which parses each of the inputs as loads says. Any other rename is a grammar error of loading. control is what the bundled bootstrap gives. It is also what the bundled bootstrap gives when a wrapper of its own stands around each of these rules.
document:
```jbogenbau
%ambiguity-resolution greedy
%features f g
%const $K (A ∪ B)
%redefine-const $K (A ∪ B ∪ ∅)
%classifier lex f? "mi" ∈ KOHA ¬g? "do" ∉ KOHA


%implies (A ∩ B) ⟹ (C ∖ D)
%rule text :: (V ∪ (($x ∧ $x.source-text.classify(lex) ⊆ W) ⟹ X)) :- $.verbatim-text | f? h! ($x:word $y:"l"="l" [("c" | "d")] [+KU "z"] {"e"} ("f" & "g") "h".."k" _Lu Sound-0061-s H "m"<¬B>) :: (T ∪ $K) | ¬f? ($z:"b" [("c" [$w:"n"])]) :: U | ("q" text-tail) %conditions (($x.source-text = "ok" ∨ $y.starts-input) ⟹ (¬($x.first-token.matches(word)) ∧ $y)), $x.tokens-after-first.begins(word), $y.source-text ∈ "a.b".split(".") %emits $x ($y) :: ($x.tags ∩ $x.source-text.classify(lex)), ε :: Y







%rule word {"w"}

%rule text-tail ε

%redefine-rule text-tail (🆓 "r")

%extend-rule text-tail "s"

%rule 🆓 "t"

```

extraParts.description: A range with a third character reads only its first two (engine §9).
A comparison with a third union reads only its first two (engine §9).
An implication with a third union reads only its first two (engine §9).
A repetition with no marker, in a shape of its own, reads its first choice as the item and its second as the separator (engine §9).
A marker before the first choice makes a left chain, wherever it stands before it (engine §9).
A marker after the first choice, with no second choice before it, makes a right chain (engine §9).
Two markers are an error of the document at the second (engine §9).
Three markers are an error of the document at the second (engine §9).
A marker after the second choice is an error of the document at that marker, since the separator has no marker (engine §9).
A third choice is a part that the reader does not read (engine §9).
An optional with two markers, in a shape of its own, is an error of the document at the second marker (engine §9).
A marker inside a wrapper rule is read through the wrapper: [+KU 'b'] is elidable, so x elides KU on a and y wins under late-elision. Read as a plain optional, it would tie (engine §9).

```jbogenbau
%ambiguity-resolution late-elision
%rule text x | y
%rule x ("a" [+KU "b"])
%rule y "a"
```

extraParts.description: A group at the head of a marked optional is an error at the [, also where the optional reads its choice through a wrapper rule: the reader looks through wrappers but not through a group (engine §9).
A tested that lacks its test is an error at the tested, before its primary, here a constant, is read (engine §9).
An optional looks up its choice before its markers: one with two markers and no choice is an error at the optional, not at the second marker (engine §9).
A repetition looks up its choices before its markers: one with two markers and no choice is an error at the repetition, not at the second marker (engine §9).
A tested looks up its test before its primary: one that lacks its test, and whose primary holds no known part, is an error at the tested, not at its primary (engine §9).
